subject: Order form & MSA — clarifying output ownership, training use, and feedback license
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@cloudscribe.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form & MSA — clarifying output ownership, training use, and feedback license

Alex — attaching our latest MSA + order form with redlines (Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf, OrderForm_CloudScribe_v2.docx). Two quick asks to help move legal along: 

1) Output ownership: CloudScribe requested a broad "ownership of outputs" line. We are fine with granting customers title to Outputs they receive from the Service for their internal business use, but we need to limit downstream productization and public resale without explicit agreement. Please confirm if the CloudScribe team can accept the attached clause that: 
   - Gives the customer ownership to Outputs generated from their Customer Data and prompts;
   - Carves out Redwood's right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement unless the customer opts-out (opt-out path in order form);

2) Training / feedback license: we propose separating a short feedback license (time-limited, nonexclusive) from the training permission. The order form currently conflates these. Our proposed orderform snippets (attached) split the items and offer an explicit opt-out for model training.

Can you ask your legal team to review the highlighted sections and confirm whether they can accept the carveouts (customer Outputs vs Redwood telemetry)? If helpful, we can do a 30-min sync this week.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf), OrderForm_CloudScribe_v2.docx (docx)

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 9 Aug 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form & MSA — clarifying output ownership, training use, and feedback license

Thanks, Hannah — appreciate the clear callouts. Quick thoughts from our side: 

- We want strong ownership language around Outputs since product teams will be building features on top of the generated content. A carveout allowing Redwood to use aggregated telemetry is probably OK, but we need assurance that "de-identified" means irreversible aggregation (no re-identification).
- Training opt-out: we expect an explicit checkbox on the order form for customers who want to opt out of model training. Does the proposed snippet show that?
- Feedback license: we need the license to be non-transferable and limited to use for improving Redwood's service to CloudScribe only (not broader commercialization) — can you confirm?

I attached our annotated redlines (CloudScribe_Redlines_annotated.docx) with inline comments. Can we do a call Monday 8/11 to close the remaining points? If Laura (or whoever on your legal team) can join, that would be helpful.

Best,
Alex
Sr. Counsel, CloudScribe

Attachment: CloudScribe_Redlines_annotated.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Order form & MSA — clarifying output ownership, training use, and feedback license

Looping Laura in for legal language. Alex — quick commercial trade we can offer to unblock:

- Customer Outputs: full ownership for CloudScribe for Outputs derived from their prompts and Customer Data for internal use and customer-facing features built atop those Outputs (we'll allow "productization" inside the customer's product), BUT Redwood retains the right to market and commercialize general improvements to the Service that are trained on aggregated, de-identified signals (not tied back to CloudScribe).
- Training opt-out: include explicit opt-out checkbox on the Order Form for training-use and telemetry; opt-out will preserve customer Outputs and still allow Redwood to collect minimal telemetry for SLO and security, subject to the data use table.
- Feedback license: propose a limited, revocable, non-transferable license to use Feedback for 12 months to improve the service; not assignable to third parties except affiliates.

I've put suggested snippet language into "proposed-orderform-snippets.txt" (attached) — it's intentionally short so legal has a clean starting point. Proposed next step: 30-min legal + product call on Monday 8/11 10:00am PT. Laura, can you confirm availability and if the attached snippets look OK from a risk perspective?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-orderform-snippets.txt (txt)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@cloudscribe.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Aug 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form & MSA — clarifying output ownership, training use, and feedback license

Alex / team — thanks for the annotated redlines. Quick legal read and proposed path to execution: 

1) Definitions: we need to make a clear distinction between "Customer Data" (data provided to the Service) and "Customer Outputs" (content returned by the Service). My proposed text (excerpt below) preserves Customer ownership of Outputs while protecting Redwood's product improvement right: 
   - "Customer Outputs" means content generated by the Service in response to Customer Data or prompts. Customer shall own Customer Outputs for its internal business purposes; provided, however, that Redwood may use Aggregated De-identified Telemetry (as defined) to improve the Service so long as such telemetry is irreversibly aggregated and cannot be re-associated with Customer or individual end users.

2) Aggregated De-identified Telemetry: add explicit description and examples (model logs, token usage histograms, anonymized error traces) and an assurance that raw prompts or customer-submitted PII will not be used to train models without explicit opt-in. We will include a short audit right for enterprise customers under the Dedicated/Private plans.

3) Training vs Feedback: accept splitting these. Proposed feedback license: 12-month, non-exclusive, revocable, non-transferable license to use Feedback to improve Redwood services for the benefit of the Customer. Training permission must be separately flagged on the Order Form as an opt-in (default = opt-in for hosted customers; explicit checkbox for opt-out request available on enterprise order forms).

4) Compliance asks: before we sign, CloudScribe requested SOC 2 evidence and a data retention table. Recommend we provide SOC 2 Type II summary and our standard data retention schedule via the link below. Also flag for procurement that enterprise deals with training opt-outs may have higher unit costs.

If CloudScribe can accept the language above, I'm comfortable moving to signature with the attached legal redline applied. If they push for a blanket transfer of Outputs (e.g., broad ability to sell generated content to third parties), we should escalate.

Proposed next steps:
- 30-min legal call Monday 8/11 10:00am PT (Laura + Alex + Hannah + Ben)
- Share SOC 2 summary and retention table during the call (https://redwood.infra/security/soc2-summary)

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
